summary: Mutation testing extracted from one project's self-propagating LEARNINGS lore into a decided, bounded protocol — shipped as the OPT-IN `with-mutation` capability profile, never as a universal gate. docs/MUTATION_TESTING.md is the protocol; scripts/mutation-run.py executes an LLM-authored mutant spec in foreground chunks and writes a write-only audit record. Neither is installed by the default profile.
decision_memo: foundry-meta/KICKOFF-phasekit-session-lifetime.md item 4. SCOPE DECIDED BEFORE BUILDING, per the kickoff's instruction: capability-profile option, matching its own recommendation. The kickoff said to STOP and ask only if I concluded it should be universal; I did not, so no question was raised.
suggested_commit_message: session lifetime: mutation testing as an opt-in protocol, not lore
reviewer_notes: Scope: opt-in. phasekit is a public curl|bash tool whose META_SPEC states it must work for someone with no orchestration layer, so mandating a heavy practice for every downstream user would be a far bigger claim than 'Foundry does this'. Pinned by tests, not just by intent: a default enrich installs neither file, and the with-mutation profile installs both.

The division of labour is the design. The LLM designs mutants (that is where all three real defects came from); the harness only executes. mutation-run.py never invents a mutant — if it did, it would generate the cheap syntactic ones good tests already catch, and the audit record would fill with noise that makes the practice look effective while catching nothing.

Chunking, not resumability, exactly as the kickoff decided. Nothing is backgrounded, so nothing can be orphaned when a turn ends — which is the failure the rest of this release exists to prevent, and the reason the original mutation run cost three sessions. The rejected resumable cache is recorded in the script, in the doc, and pinned by a test asserting no --resume/cache machinery exists.

Two false-green refusals: a budget-skipped mutant is recorded as `not_run` and never as a pass, and an ambiguous `find` (matching more than once) is an error rather than a guess, because the outcome would not say which site it referred to.

Safety: refuses a dirty tree (patch/revert in place could otherwise restore a file over uncommitted edits) and the revert is in a `finally`, so an interrupted run cannot leave a mutation behind. A stray surviving mutation in a commit is the worst thing this script could produce.

WORKFLOW_SCRIPTS had to grow to make include_scripts able to install mutation-run at all — it previously only carried run-phase and run-until-done. That is precisely what makes the script opt-in: no profile except with-mutation names it.

DOGFOODED. Ran the harness against this release's own Stop-hook tests with two mutants aimed at the subtlest properties — the block bound (>= to >) and the staleness check (dropping the -nt comparison). Both were KILLED, so those tests genuinely discriminate rather than merely execute.

deferred_items.description: Tag the next minor and push. Version chosen at tag time per the kickoff — no number was pre-assigned.
Stall watchdog should fire on the FIRST zero-commit session that also leaves a dirty tree; and the scaffold-drift signal should recognise a `phasekit upgrade` commit.

commands_run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'  -> 348 tests OK
verification.acceptance_criteria_met: the protocol specifies chunking, a budget, a write-only audit record and the LLM-designs/harness-executes split; it ships opt-in and the opt-in-ness is pinned by tests
